styles.label: Beaches
styles.blurb: Sandy coves, a long seafront promenade and boat trips to Sveti Nikola island.

styles.label: Old Town
styles.blurb: Walled stone streets, small churches and a harbour view in one walk.

styles.label: Nightlife
styles.blurb: Beach clubs by day and busy bars and clubs along the coast after dark.

stays.why: Walled-town streets, the harbour and most restaurants are a short walk away. Quiet at night, but it has steep, narrow lanes and no parking.
The main town beach, close to the centre and the promenade. Good for easy walks into town and for beach days.
A long sandy beach with many hotels and beach clubs. Best for beach-focused stays; it is a short taxi ride to the Old Town.
A quieter, small-bay area with rocky swimming spots and sea views. Good for a calm stay; expect taxi rides for nightlife.

food: Try fresh grilled fish and seafood platters at harbour restaurants in the Old Town and along the marina.
Order local black risotto (crni rižoto) or grilled squid where the menu lists it, and ask for the catch of the day.
Eat at the Old Town cafés in the morning and the seafront restaurants at sunset; prices are higher right by the walls.
Look for local bakeries and burek or pljeskavica stands for a cheap lunch away from the main promenade.
Check menus for euro prices and whether a service charge is included before you order.
more_time: Take a boat trip to Sveti Nikola island or a nearby beach. Tourist boats are not cheap, so compare prices at the marina first.
Spend a day in Herceg Novi. Intercity buses run about every 30 minutes for around €6 each way.
Visit Kotor or Perast for a historic day trip. Check bus or taxi times before you go, as schedules change by season.

recommend.why: Two nights give you a full beach day, an Old Town evening and time for a boat trip or a day trip to Kotor.

month_notes: Jan: Cold (5–11°C) with 13 rain days. Quiet off-season; many places are closed.
Feb: Cool (7–13°C) and rainy on 12 days. Good for quiet walks, not beach days.
Mar: Mild (8–15°C) with 14 rain days. Spring starts; check opening hours.
Apr: Warmer (11–18°C) with 12 rain days. Good for sightseeing and walks.
May: Pleasant (16–22°C) with 14 rain days. Sea still cool; bring a light layer.
Jun: Warm (21–27°C) with 9 rain days. Beaches and bars open; start booking early.
Jul: Hot (23–30°C) with only 5 rain days. Peak season; crowds and high prices.
Aug: Hottest month (24–31°C) with 7 rain days. Peak crowds; go to the beach early or late.
Sep: Still warm (19–26°C) with 11 rain days. Good weather with fewer crowds.
Oct: Mild (15–21°C) with 11 rain days. Good for walking and seafood.
Nov: Cool (11–17°C) with 14 rain days. Off-season; many beach venues close.
Dec: Cold (7–13°C) with 12 rain days. Quiet off-season; pack a warm jacket.

climate_guide.summary: Mediterranean climate: hot, dry summers and mild, wetter winters. The sea is warmest from July to September.

items.title: Best time: June to September
items.text: Warm days of 21–31°C and very few rainy days in July and August. Best for beaches and nightlife.

items.title: Peak heat (July and August)
items.text: Highs of 30–31°C. Swim early or late, and use shade in the Old Town.

items.title: Rain mostly in winter
items.text: Between 11 and 14 rain days a month from October to May. Pack a light waterproof jacket.

items.title: Sea temperature
items.text: Warmest from late July to September. The water is cold for most of the year.

items.title: Cool winters
items.text: Lows of 5–8°C in January and February. Many beach venues and some restaurants close.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes for summer, a warm layer for evenings, comfortable walking shoes for stone streets, and a swimsuit.

transit.best: Walk within the centre and take a metered taxi or book through MonteGO for longer trips.

modes.text: No metro or tram. Don't plan around rail.
Local buses are limited. Intercity buses leave from the bus station, about a 20-minute walk from the Old Town. Herceg Novi buses run about every 30 minutes for around €6.
Taxis cost around €5 for a ride within town. Use a metered taxi with a visible rate card, or book through MonteGO for upfront fare estimates.
Driving is hard in summer. Traffic is heavy and Old Town parking is scarce and costly. Leave the car outside the centre.
The centre is about 2 km², and the promenade links the coast. Walking is the easiest way to get around.
Tourist boats run to nearby beaches and Sveti Nikola island. They are not cheap, and there are no €1 water taxis.
